The center magnet has both a north and south polarity. The magnets in the ring also have N and S polarity, with either N or S pointing inwards. It doesn't matter which is in and which is out.

Since the center magnet has both N and S, and for the sake of this example we'll say the ring has S pointing inwards. The N on the center magnet is attracted to the S on the ring, while the S on the magnet is repelled by the S on the ring. Since the strength of the attraction is the same as the strength of the repelling you end up with circular motion as one side pulls in all directions while the other side pushes in all directions. The spinning is the most stable state the magnet can achieve in that situation.

What's really cool is that if you can turn the ring on and off by using electromagnets instead of regular magnets, and hook the center magnet up to a wheel or cog, you've created an electric motor.
